title: Day 28 and day 29 terms in February, leap year and not
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have work order 1, complete and ready to invoice, for a customer on the shop's own term due on day 28 of the following month.
  • Have work order 2, complete and ready to invoice, for a customer on the shop's own term due on day 29 of the following month.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1's Finance tab.
  2. Set Invoice Date to Jan 20, 2027.
  3. Open work order 2's Finance tab.
  4. Set Invoice Date to Jan 20, 2027.
  5. Set Invoice Date to Jan 20, 2028.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The invoice preview shows.

Step 2:

  • The Due date reads Feb 28, 2027 (day 28 exists in every February).

Step 3:

  • The invoice preview shows.

Step 4:

  • The Due date reads Feb 28, 2027 (2027 has no Feb 29, so the last day is used).

Step 5:

  • The Due date reads Feb 29, 2028 (2028 is a leap year, so day 29 exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R3: “When the following month is shorter than the term's day, the due date is that month's last day: day 31 invoiced in October is due Nov 30; day 30 or 31 invoiced in January is due Feb 28 (Feb 29 in a leap year); day 31 invoiced in March is due Apr 30.”
